facts.statement: The genus Iguanodon was named in 1825 by English geologist Gideon Mantell based on fossils found in England.
facts.quote: The genus was named in 1825 by English geologist Gideon Mantell, based on fossil specimens found in England

facts.statement: Iguanodon was the second dinosaur genus formally named based on fossil specimens, following Megalosaurus.
facts.quote: Iguanodon was the second type of dinosaur formally named based on fossil specimens, after Megalosaurus

facts.statement: Iguanodon was a large, bulky herbivore that could reach lengths of 9 to 11 meters and weigh up to 4.5 metric tons.
facts.quote: Iguanodon was a large, bulky herbivore, measuring up to 9 - 11 m in length and 4.5 MT in body mass

facts.statement: Iguanodon possessed large thumb spikes likely used for defense and long, prehensile fifth fingers used for foraging.
facts.quote: Distinctive features include large thumb spikes, which were possibly used for defense against predators, combined with long prehensile fifth fingers able to forage for food

facts.statement: A popular legend claims Mary Ann Mantell discovered the first Iguanodon teeth in Tilgate Forest in 1822, though evidence suggests Gideon Mantell found them himself.
facts.quote: The story posits that Gideon Mantell's wife, Mary Ann, discovered the first teeth of an Iguanodon in the strata of Tilgate Forest in Whitemans Green, Sussex, England, in 1822

facts.statement: Samuel Stutchbury identified the resemblance between Iguanodon teeth and those of an iguana at the Royal College of Surgeons in September 1824.
facts.quote: In September 1824 he visited the Royal College of Surgeons but at first failed to find comparable teeth. However, assistant-curator Samuel Stutchbury recognised that they resembled those of an iguana he had recently prepared, albeit twenty times longer

facts.statement: Gideon Mantell formally published his findings on Iguanodon on February 10, 1825, by presenting a paper to the Royal Society of London.
facts.quote: Mantell formally published his findings on 10 February 1825, when he presented a paper on the remains to the Royal Society of London

facts.statement: Early reconstructions of Iguanodon incorrectly placed a horn on its nose, which was later identified as a modified thumb.
facts.quote: The most famous of which was the placement of what he thought was a horn on the nose

facts.statement: Iguanodon belongs to the larger group Iguanodontia, which also includes duck-billed hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: The genus Iguanodon belongs to the larger group Iguanodontia, along with the duck-billed hadrosaurs

facts.statement: The originally described type species, Iguanodon anglicus, is now considered a nomen dubium and is not valid.
facts.quote: the originally described type species of Iguanodon, I. anglicus is now a nomen dubium, and not valid

facts.statement: The Maidstone specimen, known as the "Mantel-piece" and labeled NHMUK 3741, was excluded from the genus Iguanodon.
facts.quote: The Maidstone specimen, also known as Gideon Mantell's "Mantel-piece", and formally labelled NHMUK 3741 was subsequently excluded from Iguanodon

facts.statement: The Maidstone specimen is classified as cf. Mantellisaurus by some researchers, while others proposed it as the holotype of Mantellodon carpenteri, though this classification is considered dubious.
facts.quote: It is classified as cf. Mantellisaurus by McDonald (2012); as cf. Mantellisaurus atherfieldensis by Norman (2012); and made the holotype of a separate species Mantellodon carpenteri by Paul (2012), but this is considered dubious

facts.statement: Gideon Mantell realized in 1849 that Iguanodon had slender forelimbs rather than being heavy, pachyderm-like animals.
facts.quote: In 1849, a few years before his death in 1852, Mantell realised that iguanodonts were not heavy, pachyderm-like animals, as Owen was putting forward, but had slender forelimbs.

facts.statement: The largest known find of Iguanodon remains occurred on February 28, 1878, in a coal mine at Bernissart, Belgium, at a depth of 322 meters.
facts.quote: The largest find of Iguanodon remains to that date occurred on 28 February 1878 in a coal mine at Bernissart in Belgium, at a depth of 322 m, when two mineworkers, Jules Créteur and Alphonse Blanchard, accidentally hit on a skeleton that they initially took for petrified wood.

facts.statement: At least 38 Iguanodon individuals were uncovered in the Bernissart mine, most of which were adults.
facts.quote: At least 38 Iguanodon individuals were uncovered, most of which were adults.

facts.statement: Specimen IRSNB 1551 was initially referred to I. mantelli but is now classified as Mantellisaurus atherfieldensis.
facts.quote: One specimen, IRSNB 1551, was at first referred to the nebulous, gracile I. mantelli, but is currently referred to Mantellisaurus atherfieldensis.

facts.statement: Between December 1935 and August 1936, the Brussels museum treated the fossils with alcohol, arsenic, and 390 kilograms of shellac.
facts.quote: From December 1935 to August 1936 the staff at the museum in Brussels treated the problem with a combination of alcohol, arsenic, and 390 kilograms of shellac.

facts.statement: The Bernissart fossils underwent a third conservation round from 2003 to May 2007, involving the removal of previous treatments and impregnation with modern glues.
facts.quote: The fossils entered a third round of conservation from 2003 until May 2007, when the shellac, hide glue and gelatine were removed and impregnated with polyvinyl acetate and cyanoacrylate and epoxy glues.

facts.statement: The species I. atherfieldensis was named in 1925 by R. W. Hooley based on a specimen from Atherfield Point on the Isle of Wight.
facts.quote: A new species that would become the subject of much study and taxonomic controversy, I. atherfieldensis, was named in 1925 by R. W. Hooley, for a specimen collected at Atherfield Point on the Isle of Wight.

facts.statement: A find in Nehden, Germany, included at least 15 individuals ranging from 2 to 8 meters in length, mostly Mantellisaurus (formerly I. atherfieldensis) with some I. bernissartensis.
facts.quote: At least 15 individuals, from 2 to 8 m long, have been found here, most of the individuals belong to the related Mantellisaurus (described as I. atherfieldensis, at that time believed to be another species of Iguanodon). but some are of I. bernissartensis.

facts.statement: With a straight tail and back, Iguanodon likely walked with its body held horizontally to the ground, using its arms to support itself if necessary.
facts.quote: With its correct, straight tail and back, the animal would have walked with its body held horizontal to the ground, arms in place to support the body if needed.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Dollo's reconstruction of Iguanodon was accurate, as the tail was likely straight rather than bent, supported by evidence of ossified tendons.
facts.quote: A major flaw with Dollo's reconstruction was the bend he introduced into the tail. This organ was more or less straight, as shown by the skeletons he was excavating, and the presence of ossified tendons.

facts.statement: Benjamin Waterhouse Hawkins held a banquet for twenty people inside the standing Iguanodon sculpture before it was completed.
facts.quote: Before the sculpture of the standing iguanodont was completed, he held a banquet for twenty inside it.

facts.statement: Researchers processed Iguanodon bones in 2003 to search for remnant proteins.
facts.quote: In research by Graham Embery et al. (2003), Iguanodon bones were processed to look for remnant proteins.

facts.statement: Identifiable remains of bone proteins like phosphoproteins and proteoglycans were found in an Iguanodon rib.
facts.quote: In this research, identifiable remains of typical bone proteins, such as phosphoproteins and proteoglycans, were found in a rib.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul split I. atherfieldensis into the separate genus Mantellisaurus in 2007.
facts.quote: In 2007, Gregory S. Paul split I. atherfieldensis into a new, separate genus, Mantellisaurus which has been generally accepted.

facts.statement: Fragmentary iguanodontid material was described from the upper Barremian Paris Basin in Auxerre, Burgundy, in 2009.
facts.quote: In 2009 fragmentary iguanodontid material was described from upper Barremian Paris Basin deposits in Auxerre, Burgundy.

facts.statement: David Norman split the Valanginian species I. dawsoni and I. fittoni into the genera Barilium and Hypselospinus in 2010.
facts.quote: In 2010, David Norman split the Valanginian species I. dawsoni and I. fittoni into Barilium and Hypselospinus respectively.

facts.statement: The genus Delapparentia was named in 2011 for a Spanish specimen originally thought to be I. bernissartensis.
facts.quote: In 2011, a new genus Delapparentia was named for a specimen in Spain that was originally thought to belong to I. bernissartensis.

facts.statement: The species I. galvensis was named in 2015 based on 13 juvenile individuals found in the Camarillas Formation near Galve, Spain.
facts.quote: In 2015 a new species of Iguanodon, I. galvensis, was named based on material including 13 juvenile (perinate) individuals found in the Camarillas Formation near Galve, Spain.

facts.statement: Iguanodon were bulky herbivores capable of shifting between bipedal and quadrupedal locomotion.
facts.quote: Iguanodon were bulky herbivores that could shift from bipedality to quadrupedality.

facts.statement: The species I. bernissartensis is estimated to have been about 9 meters long as an adult, with a maximum reported length of 11 meters.
facts.quote: The only well-supported species, I. bernissartensis, is estimated to have measured about 9 m long as an adult, with some specimens possibly as long as 13 m, although this is likely an overestimate, given that the maximum body length of I. bernissartensis is reported to be 11 m.

facts.statement: While Gregory S. Paul suggested an average mass of 3.08 metric tons, 3D modeling suggests an average I. bernissartensis weighing close to 3.8 metric tons.
facts.quote: Although Gregory S. Paul suggested a body mass of 3.08 MT on average, constructing a 3D mathematical model and employing allometry-based estimate suggests an I. bernissartensis close to 8 m long (smaller than average) weighs close to 3.8 MT in body mass.

facts.statement: Large individuals of Iguanodon would have weighed approximately 4.5 metric tons.
facts.quote: Such large individuals would have weighed approximately 4.5 MT.

facts.statement: The arms of I. bernissartensis were long, reaching up to 75% of leg length, with robust hands built to bear weight on the three central fingers.
facts.quote: The arms of I. bernissartensis were long (up to 75% the length of the legs) and robust, with rather inflexible hands built so that the three central fingers could bear weight.

facts.statement: Iguanodon thumbs were conical spikes that projected away from the three main digits.
facts.quote: The thumbs were conical spikes that stuck out away from the three main digits.

facts.statement: The little finger of Iguanodon was elongated and dextrous, likely used for manipulating objects.
facts.quote: The little finger was elongated and dextrous, and could have been used to manipulate objects.

facts.statement: The phalangeal formula of Iguanodon is 2-3-3-2-4, indicating the number of bones in each digit from innermost to outermost.
facts.quote: The phalangeal formula is 2-3-3-2-4, meaning that the innermost finger (phalange) has two bones, the next has three, etc.

facts.statement: Iguanodon had large, tall, narrow skulls with toothless keratin-covered beaks and large, closely packed teeth resembling those of iguanas.
facts.quote: These animals had large, tall but narrow skulls, with toothless beaks probably covered with keratin, and teeth like those of iguanas, as the name suggests, but much larger and more closely packed.

facts.statement: Iguanodon gives its name to the clade Iguanodontia, a populous group of ornithopods known from the Middle Jurassic to the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Iguanodon gives its name to the unranked clade Iguanodontia, a very populous group of ornithopods with many species known from the Middle Jurassic to the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Cladistic analyses showed that the traditional family Iguanodontidae was paraphyletic, with members falling at different points relative to hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: With the advent of cladistic analyses, Iguanodontidae as traditionally construed was shown to be paraphyletic, and these animals are recognised to fall at different points in relation to hadrosaurs on a cladogram, instead of in a single distinct clade.

facts.statement: The modern concept of the family Iguanodontidae currently includes only the genus Iguanodon.
facts.quote: Essentially, the modern concept of Iguanodontidae currently includes only Iguanodon.

facts.statement: The exact function of Iguanodon thumb spikes is debated, with hypotheses suggesting they were used for defense or foraging.
facts.quote: Later fossils revealed the true nature of the thumb spikes, although their exact function is still debated. They could have been used for defense, or for foraging for food.

facts.statement: In 2026, Rotatori and colleagues suggested that Delapparentia is a distinct taxon related to Magnamanus and I. galvensis, proposing a new genus name for the latter.
facts.quote: In 2026, Rotatori and colleagues suggested that Delapperantia is a distinct taxon more closely related to Magnamanus and "I." galvensis, the latter of which they suggested that a new genus name would be required.

facts.statement: Paleontologists have informally disagreed with the methodology used to assign I. galvensis to the genus Paulodon.
facts.quote: although paleontologists have informally disagreed with the methodology behind the paper.

facts.statement: The International Commission on Zoological Nomenclature officially changed the type species of Iguanodon to I. bernissartensis in March 2000, designating IRSNB 1534 as the new holotype.
facts.quote: In March 2000, the International Commission on Zoological Nomenclature changed the type species to the much better known I. bernissartensis, with the new holotype being IRSNB 1534.

facts.statement: The original type specimen, a single tooth, is held at Te Papa Tongarewa in Wellington, New Zealand, but is not currently on display.
facts.quote: The original Iguanodon tooth is held at Te Papa Tongarewa, the national museum of New Zealand in Wellington, although it is not on display.

facts.statement: Only one species, I. bernissartensis, described by George Albert Boulenger in 1881, is currently considered valid within the genus Iguanodon.
facts.quote: Only one species assigned to Iguanodon is still considered to be valid. I. bernissartensis, described by George Albert Boulenger in 1881, is the type species for the genus.

facts.statement: I. bernissartensis is best known from numerous skeletons found in the Sainte-Barbe Clays Formation at Bernissart, with additional remains found across Europe.
facts.quote: This species is best known for the many skeletons discovered in the Sainte-Barbe Clays Formation at Bernissart, but is also known from remains across Europe.

facts.statement: I. seelyi, described by John Hulke in 1882, has been synonymized with I. bernissartensis, although this classification is not universally accepted by all researchers.
facts.quote: I. seelyi (also incorrectly spelled I. seeleyi), described by John Hulke in 1882, has also been synonymised with Iguanodon bernissartensis, though this is not universally accepted.

facts.statement: I. seelyi was discovered in Brook on the Isle of Wight and named after Charles Seely MP, the Liberal politician and philanthropist whose estate contained the fossil.
facts.quote: It was discovered in Brook, on the Isle of Wight, and named after Charles Seely MP, Liberal politician and philanthropist, on whose estate it was found.

facts.statement: I. albinus, described by Antonin Fritsch in 1893, is now considered a dubious nondinosaurian reptile known as Albisaurus albinus.
facts.quote: I. albinus (or Albisaurus scutifer), described by Czech palaeontologist Antonin Fritsch in 1893, is a dubious nondinosaurian reptile now known as Albisaurus albinus.

facts.statement: I. atherfieldensis, described by R.W. Hooley in 1925, was renamed Mantellisaurus atherfieldensis in 2007 after being found to be smaller and less robust than I. bernissartensis.
facts.quote: I. atherfieldensis, described by R.W. Hooley in 1925, was smaller and less robust than I. bernissartensis, with longer neural spines. It was renamed Mantellisaurus atherfieldensis in 2007.

facts.statement: I. dawsoni, described by Lydekker in 1888 from the Wadhurst Clay in East Sussex, is now the type species of the genus Barilium.
facts.quote: I. dawsoni, described by Lydekker in 1888, is known from two partial skeletons found in East Sussex, England, from the middle Valanginian-age Lower Cretaceous Wadhurst Clay. It is now the type species of Barilium.

facts.statement: I. fittoni, described by Lydekker in 1889 from the Wadhurst Clay, is now the type species of the genus Hypselospinus.
facts.quote: I. fittoni was described by Lydekker in 1889. Like I. dawsoni, this species was described from the Wadhurst Clay of East Sussex. It is now the type species of Hypselospinus.

facts.statement: I. hilli, coined by Edwin Tully Newton in 1892, was once considered an early hadrosaurid but is now placed as indeterminate beyond Hadrosauroidea.
facts.quote: I. hilli, coined by Edwin Tully Newton in 1892 for a tooth from the early Cenomanian Upper Cretaceous Lower Chalk of Hertfordshire, has been considered an early hadrosaurid of some sort. However, recent work places it as indeterminate beyond Hadrosauroidea outside Hadrosauridae.

facts.statement: I. lakotaensis, described by David B. Weishampel and Philip R. Bjork in 1989, is the only well-accepted North American species of Iguanodon, based on a partial skull from the Lakota Formation of South Dakota.
facts.quote: I. lakotaensis was described by David B. Weishampel and Philip R. Bjork in 1989. The only well-accepted North American species of Iguanodon, I. lakotaensis was described from a partial skull from the Barremian-age Lower Cretaceous Lakota Formation of South Dakota.

facts.statement: I. orientalis, described by A. K. Rozhdestvensky in 1952, was renamed Altirhinus kurzanovi in 1998 after a skull with a distinctive arched snout was reassigned to it.
facts.quote: I. orientalis, described by A. K. Rozhdestvensky in 1952, was based on poor material, but a skull with a distinctive arched snout that had been assigned to it was renamed Altirhinus kurzanovi in 1998.

facts.statement: I. prestwichii, described by John Hulke in 1880, has been reassigned to either Camptosaurus prestwichii or its own genus, Cumnoria.
facts.quote: I. prestwichii (also spelled I. prestwichi), described by John Hulke in 1880, has been reassigned to Camptosaurus prestwichii or to its own genus Cumnoria.

facts.statement: I. foxii was originally described by Thomas Henry Huxley in 1869 as the type species of Hypsilophodon, later reassigned to Iguanodon by Owen, but this assignment was soon overturned.
facts.quote: I. foxii (also spelled I. foxi) was originally described by Thomas Henry Huxley in 1869 as the type species of Hypsilophodon; Owen (1873 or 1874) reassigned it to Iguanodon, but his assignment was soon overturned.

facts.statement: I. major, named by Justin Delair in 1966 based on vertebrae originally described by Owen in 1842, is considered a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: I. major, a species named by Justin Delair in 1966, based on vertebrae from the Isle of Wight and Sussex originally described by Owen in 1842 as a species of Streptospondylus, S. major, is a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: I. anglicus, described by Friedrich Holl in 1829, was the original type species of Iguanodon but was later replaced by I. bernissartensis.
facts.quote: I. anglicus, described by Friedrich Holl in 1829, is the original type species of Iguanodon, but, as discussed above, was replaced by I. bernissartensis.

facts.statement: Iguanodon had a toothless, scoop-shaped lower jaw symphysis that resembles that of two-toed sloths and the extinct ground sloth Mylodon.
facts.quote: the toothless, scoop-shaped form of the lower jaw symphysis, which he found best compared to that of the two-toed sloth and the extinct ground sloth Mylodon.

facts.statement: Iguanodon possessed a flexible little finger used to manipulate objects while gathering food.
facts.quote: Its food gathering would have been aided by its flexible little finger, which could have been used to manipulate objects, unlike the other fingers.

facts.statement: Larger species like Iguanodon bernissartensis could reach foliage from 4 to 5 meters high.
facts.quote: The size of the larger species, such as I. bernissartensis, would have allowed them access to food from ground level to tree foliage at 4 – 5 m high.

facts.statement: David Norman suggested Iguanodon ate horsetails, cycads, and conifers, while other theories link iguanodonts to angiosperm plants in the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: A diet of horsetails, cycads, and conifers was suggested by David Norman, although iguanodonts in general have been tied to the advance of angiosperm plants in the Cretaceous due to the dinosaurs' inferred low-browsing habits.

facts.statement: Due to its size and abundance, Iguanodon is considered a dominant medium to large herbivore in its ecological communities.
facts.quote: Whatever its exact diet, due to its size and abundance, Iguanodon is regarded as a dominant medium to large herbivore for its ecological communities.

facts.statement: Early reconstructions depicted Iguanodon as a quadrupedal beast with a horn on its nose.
facts.quote: Iguanodon was initially portrayed as a quadrupedal horn-nosed beast.

facts.statement: The discovery of Bernissart skeletons revealed that Iguanodon was bipedal.
facts.quote: Its bipedal nature was revealed with the discovery of the Bernissart skeletons.

facts.statement: Iguanodon's long tail was stiffened by ossified tendons.
facts.quote: The long tail was stiffened with ossified tendons.

facts.statement: Iguanodon had a relatively long three-toed foot and walked in a digitigrade fashion using both hands and feet.
facts.quote: The three-toed pes (foot) of Iguanodon was relatively long, and when walking, both the hand and the foot would have been used in a digitigrade fashion (walking on the fingers and toes).

facts.statement: Iguanodon could reach a maximum speed of 24 km/h when moving bipedally but could not gallop as a quadruped.
facts.quote: The maximum speed of Iguanodon has been estimated at 24 km/h, which would have been as a biped; it would not have been able to gallop as a quadruped.

facts.statement: Juvenile Iguanodon bernissartensis had shorter arms, measuring 60% of hindlimb length compared to 70% in adults.
facts.quote: juvenile I. bernissartensis have shorter arms than adults (60% of hindlimb length versus 70% for adults).

facts.statement: Footprints assigned to the ichnogenus Iguanodon are found across Europe, Spitsbergen, Svalbard, and Norway.
facts.quote: Tracks assigned to the ichnogenus Iguanodon are known from locations including places in Europe where the body fossil Iguanodon is known, to Spitsbergen, Svalbard, Norway.

facts.statement: Originally thought to be on the nose, the thumb spike of Iguanodon was correctly identified as a modified thumb on the hand by Dollo.
facts.quote: Although it was originally placed on the animal's nose by Mantell, the complete Bernissart specimens allowed Dollo to place it correctly on the hand, as a modified thumb.

facts.statement: Iguanodon's thumb spike is interpreted as a weapon against predators, a tool for breaking seeds and fruits, or a defense against other Iguanodon.
facts.quote: This thumb is typically interpreted as a close-quarter stiletto-like weapon against predators, although it could also have been used to break into seeds and fruits, or against other Iguanodon.

facts.statement: A hypothesis suggesting the thumb spike was attached to a venom gland has been rejected due to the spike being solid and lacking grooves for venom conduction.
facts.quote: One author has suggested that the spike was attached to a venom gland, but this has not been accepted, as the spike was not hollow, nor were there any grooves on the spike for conducting venom.

facts.statement: While Bernissart fossils show multiple mortality events within 10 to 100 years, this does not necessarily indicate Iguanodon were herding animals.
facts.quote: According to this interpretation, at least three occasions of mortality are recorded, and though numerous individuals would have died in a geologically short time span (?10–100 years), this does not necessarily mean these Iguanodon were herding animals.

facts.statement: The scarcity of juvenile remains at the Bernissart site argues against Iguanodon being herding animals.
facts.quote: An argument against herding is that juvenile remains are very uncommon at this site, unlike modern cases with herd mortality.

facts.statement: The Nehden fossil site may represent herding behavior, showing a mix of ages and species confined to a specific geographic area.
facts.quote: The Nehden find, however, with its greater span of individual ages, more even mix of Dollodon or Mantellisaurus to Iguanodon bernissartensis, and confined geographic nature, may record mortality of herding animals migrating through rivers.

facts.statement: The idea that I. atherfieldensis or Dollodon represented a female sex of the larger I. bernissartensis is no longer supported by scientific consensus.
facts.quote: At one time, it was suggested that the Bernissart I. "mantelli", or I. atherfieldensis (Dollodon and Mantellisaurus, respectively) represented a sex, possibly female, of the larger and more robust, possibly male, I. bernissartensis. However, this is not supported today.

facts.statement: A 2017 analysis revealed significant individual variation in the limbs and spinal column of Iguanodon bernissartensis.
facts.quote: A 2017 analysis showed that I. bernissartensis does exhibit a large level of individual variation in both its limbs (scapula, humerus, thumb claw, ilium, ischium, femur, tibia) and spinal column (axis, sacrum, tail vertebrae).

facts.statement: Isotope analysis suggests Iguanodon was not a migratory species and had a limited geographic range.
facts.quote: The limited range of Sr isotope composition combined with broad range of O isotope composition suggests Iguanodon wasn't a migratory species and had a limited range.

facts.statement: A fossil specimen of Iguanodon shows evidence of a fractured hip bone and an injury to the ischium.
facts.quote: Evidence of a fractured hip bone was found in a specimen of Iguanodon, which had an injury to its ischium.

facts.statement: Two other Iguanodon individuals exhibited osteoarthritis, indicated by bone overgrowths known as osteophytes in their anklebones.
facts.quote: Two other individuals were observed with signs of osteoarthritis as evidenced by bone overgrowths in their anklebones which are called osteophytes.

facts.statement: Iguanodon was discovered in 1822 and formally described in 1825 by the English geologist Gideon Mantell.
facts.quote: Descubierto en 1822 y descrito tres años más tarde en 1825 por el geólogo inglés Gideon Mantell

facts.statement: Iguanodon is one of the three genera originally used to define the group Dinosauria, alongside Megalosaurus and Hylaeosaurus.
facts.quote: Junto con Megalosaurus y Hylaeosaurus, es uno de los tres géneros usados originalmente para definir Dinosauria.

facts.statement: Iguanodon is characterized by large thumb claws that were likely used for defense against predators.
facts.quote: La principal característica de Iguanodon son sus grandes garras en los pulgares, que fueron utilizados posiblemente para defenderse de los depredadores

facts.statement: Iguanodon possessed long, grasping fifth toes capable of searching for food.
facts.quote: combinadas con los quintos dedos prensiles largos capaces de buscar comida

facts.statement: Iguanodon lived during the early Lower Cretaceous period, between 126 and 120 million years ago (Barremian to Aptian stages), in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivieron a principios del período Cretácico Inferior, entre 126 a 120 millones de años, entre el Barremiense y el Aptiense, en lo que hoy es Europa.

facts.statement: Iguanodon was a robust herbivore capable of alternating between bipedal and quadrupedal locomotion.
facts.quote: Iguanodon fue un robusto herbívoro que podía alternar entre las marchas bípeda y cuadrúpeda.

facts.statement: Adults of the best-known species, I. bernissartensis, are estimated to have weighed an average of 3 tons and measured about 10 meters long, reaching up to 13 meters in some cases.
facts.quote: Se ha estimado que los adultos de la especie mejor conocida, I. bernissartensis, pesaban un promedio de 3 toneladas, y medían cerca de 10 metros de largo, pudiendo alcanzar en algunos casos los 13 metros.

facts.statement: The spine and tail of Iguanodon were reinforced and stiffened by cylindrical ossified tendons that are often omitted in skeletal mounts and drawings.
facts.quote: La espina dorsal y la cola estaban reforzadas y rigificadas por tendones osificados cilíndricos, que se omiten generalmente en los montajes y dibujos esqueléticos.

facts.statement: The genus Iguanodon was established by Mantell in 1825.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Mantell, 1825

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Iguanodon is Iguanodon bernissartensis.
facts.quote: type_species: Iguanodon bernissartensis

facts.statement: Iguanodon belongs to the family Iguanodontidae.
facts.quote: familia: Iguanodontidae

facts.statement: Iguanodon galvensis was described by Verdú et al. in 2015 as a subdivision of the genus.
facts.quote: subdivision: Iguanodon galvensis Verdú et al., 2015

facts.statement: Iguanodon were large and robust herbivores.
facts.quote: Fueron herbívoros grandes y robustos.

facts.statement: Iguanodon had a large, high, and narrow skull with a toothless beak likely covered in keratin.
facts.quote: Este género tenía un cráneo grande, alto pero estrecho, con un desdentado pico cubierto probablemente con queratina

facts.statement: Its teeth were similar to those of an iguana but much larger and packed together.
facts.quote: los dientes como los de una iguana, pero mucho más grandes y juntos en paquetes

facts.statement: This structure caused the lower surfaces of upper teeth to rub against the upper surfaces of lower teeth, grinding food like mammals.
facts.quote: Esto causaría que las superficies más bajas de los dientes superiores frotaran contra la superficie superior de los dientes de la mandíbula, moliendo cualquier cosa entre ellos

facts.statement: Because its teeth were constantly replaced, the animal could use this grinding mechanism for its entire life.
facts.quote: Debido a que los dientes siempre eran sustituidos, el animal habría podido utilizar este mecanismo toda su vida

facts.statement: Iguanodon possessed a robust chewing apparatus with dentition typical of a herbivorous reptile.
facts.quote: Iguanodon poseía un robusto aparato masticador, dotado con la dentición típica de un reptil herbívoro

facts.statement: Iguanodon had only one replacement tooth for each tooth in use, unlike hadrosaurs which had multiple rows.
facts.quote: Iguanodon tenía un único diente de reemplazo por cada pieza dentaria en uso

facts.statement: It possessed 29 teeth in each upper jaw (58 total) and 25 teeth in each lower jaw (50 total).
facts.quote: Poseían 29 dientes en cada maxilar, 58 dientes superiores, y 25 en cada dentario, 50 dientes inferiores

facts.statement: Its legs were powerful but not suited for running, and it had three toes on each foot.
facts.quote: Las piernas eran poderosas, pero no aptas para la carrera, y tenían tres dedos en cada pie

facts.statement: Its arms were long, reaching up to 75% of the leg length in I. bernissartensis, and were robust.
facts.quote: Los brazos eran largos, hasta 75% de la longitud de las piernas en I. bernissartensis y robustos

facts.statement: The little finger (digit V) was elongated and flexible, likely used for manipulating objects.
facts.quote: El dedo meñique, el dedo V, era alargado y flexible, y habría podido ser utilizado para manipular objetos

facts.statement: Evidence of a broken hip bone with a lesion on the ischium was found in one Iguanodon specimen.
facts.quote: Se encontró evidencia de una fractura de hueso de la cadera en un espécimen de Iguanodon, que tenía una lesión en su isquion

facts.statement: Two other individuals showed signs of osteoarthritis indicated by bone growths on their ankles called osteophytes.
facts.quote: Otros dos individuos se observaron con signos de osteoartritis como lo demuestran los crecimientos óseos en sus tobillos que se llaman osteofitos

facts.statement: A characteristic of Iguanodon is its large thumb, whose second phalanx formed a large, well-developed conical claw.
facts.quote: Una de las características de Iguanodon es el gran dedo pulgar, dedo I o pollex, cuya segunda falange formaba gran una garra cónica, muy desarrollada

facts.statement: The thumbs pointed outward, perpendicular to the three central fingers.
facts.quote: Los pulgares estaban dirigidos hacia fuera, perpendiculares a los tres dedos centrales

facts.statement: This thumb is traditionally explained as a defensive element against predators or other Iguanodon.
facts.quote: Este pulgar es tradicionalmente explicado como un elemento defensivo contra los predadores o contra otros Iguanodon

facts.statement: It may also have used the thumb to break seeds and fruits.
facts.quote: aunque pudo usarlo también para partir semillas y frutas

facts.statement: It has been proposed that the claw was associated with a venom gland, but this hypothesis is disputed.
facts.quote: Se ha propuesto también la posibilidad de que la garra estuviera asociada a una glándula venenosa, pero la hipótesis está en entredicho

facts.statement: In initial reconstructions, Mantell confused the last phalanx of the thumb with a horn placed on the nose.
facts.quote: En las reconstrucciones iniciales Mantell confundió la última falange del pulgar con un cuerno que ubicó sobre la nariz

facts.statement: Iguanodon was represented with a rhinoceros-like appearance in early reconstructions until complete specimens were found in Bernissart.
facts.quote: así, con aspecto de rinoceronte, apareció representado Iguanodon en las primeras recreaciones, hasta que se hallaron los ejemplares completos en Bernissart

facts.statement: Dollo realized the error and placed the bone in the correct location of the hand, a modified thumb.
facts.quote: y Dollo se dio cuenta del error, colocando el hueso en el lugar correcto de la mano, un pulgar modificado

facts.statement: One of the first details noted about Iguanodon was that it had the teeth of a herbivorous reptile.
facts.quote: Uno de los primeros detalles notados sobre Iguanodon fue que tenía los dientes de un reptil herbívoro

facts.statement: The skull was structured so that when closing, the bones holding the teeth in the upper jaw would bend.
facts.quote: El cráneo estaba estructurado de tal manera que, al cerrarse, los huesos que sujetaban los dientes en la mandíbula superior se doblarían

facts.statement: This caused the lower surfaces of upper jaw teeth to rub against the upper surfaces of lower jaw teeth, crushing anything trapped between them.
facts.quote: Esto causaría que las superficies inferiores de los dientes de la mandíbula superior frotaran contra la superficie superior de los dientes de la mandíbula inferior, triturando cualquier cosa atrapada en el medio

facts.statement: Because teeth were always replaced, the animal could have used this mechanism throughout its life.
facts.quote: Debido a que los dientes siempre fueron reemplazados, el animal pudo haber usado este mecanismo durante toda su vida

facts.statement: It could eat tough plant material.
facts.quote: podría comer material vegetal resistente

facts.statement: The front ends of the animal's jaws had no teeth and were angled with bony nodes.
facts.quote: los extremos frontales de las mandíbulas del animal no tenían dientes y estaban inclinados con nodos óseos

facts.statement: This provided a margin likely covered and elongated by keratinous material to form a cropping beak.
facts.quote: proporcionando un margen aproximado que probablemente fue cubierto y alargado por un material queratinoso para formar un pico de cultivo

facts.statement: Its food collection would have been helped by its flexible little finger.
facts.quote: Su recolección de alimentos se habría ayudado con su dedo meñique flexible

facts.statement: The size of the largest species, like I. bernissartensis, would have allowed it to access food from the ground up to 4 to 5 meters high in trees.
facts.quote: El tamaño de las especies más grandes, como I. bernissartensis, les habría permitido acceder a los alimentos desde el nivel del suelo hasta el follaje de los árboles a una altura de 4 a 5 metros

facts.statement: David Norman suggested a diet of horsetails, cycads, and conifers.
facts.quote: David Norman sugirió una dieta de colas de caballo, cícadas y coníferas

facts.statement: However, iguanodontians in general have been related to the rise of angiosperm plants in the Cretaceous due to inferred dinosaur habits.
facts.quote: aunque los iguanodontes en general se han relacionado con el avance de las plantas de angiospermas en el Cretácico debido a los hábitos inferidos de los dinosaurios

facts.statement: However, the evidence is not conclusive regarding the specific diet.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la evidencia no es concluyente

facts.statement: Regardless of its exact diet, due to its size and abundance, Iguanodon is considered a dominant large herbivore in its ecological communities.
facts.quote: Cualquiera que sea su dieta exacta, debido a su tamaño y abundancia, Iguanodon es considerado como un medio dominante a gran herbívoro para sus comunidades ecológicas

facts.statement: Iguanodontians in general are related to the advance of angiosperm plants in the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: los iguanodontes en general se han relacionado con el avance de las plantas de angiospermas en el Cretácico

facts.statement: A specimen was considered a juvenile Mantellisaurus atherfieldensis or an undetermined Mantellisaurus species, but it is indeterminate beyond Iguanodontia.
facts.quote: Se consideró un espécimen juvenil de Mantellisaurus atherfieldensis, o una especie no determinada de Mantellisaurus, pero es indeterminado más allá de Iguanodontia

facts.statement: "Proiguanodon" is considered invalid; named by van den Broeck in 1900, it would also belong to Iguanodon.
facts.quote: "Proiguanodon": considerado inválido , nombrado por van den Broeck, en 1900 también pertenecería a iguanodon

facts.statement: The following cladogram follows an analysis by Andrew McDonald from 2012.
facts.quote: El siguiente cladograma sigue un análisis de Andrew McDonald de 2012

facts.statement: Fossil evidence from Nehden showing a wide range of ages suggests Iguanodon bernissartensis may have lived in groups.
facts.quote: Parece que Iguanodon bernissartensis pudo haber tenido hábitos gregarios, pues los hallazgos de Nehden muestran un amplio abanico de edades individuales

facts.statement: New analyses indicate at least three high-mortality events occurred over a geologically brief period of 10 to 100 years, though this does not necessarily prove herd living.
facts.quote: Según los nuevos análisis, se registran por lo menos tres sucesos de alta mortalidad y, aunque numerosos individuos habrían muerto en un periodo geológicamente breve, de entre 10 a 100 años, no prueba necesariamente que estos iguanodontes vivieran en manadas

facts.statement: Researchers suggest these animals were likely victims of periodic sudden floods, with carcasses accumulating in lake or swamp areas.
facts.quote: Eran más probablemente víctimas de inundaciones repentinas periódicas, cuyos cadáveres se acumulaban en una zona lacustre o pantanosa

facts.statement: Unlike other gregarious herbivores, there is no evidence supporting marked sexual dimorphism in Iguanodon.
facts.quote: A diferencia de otros herbívoros gregarios no hay evidencias que apoyen un marcado dimorfismo sexual

facts.statement: It was once suggested that smaller species from Bernissart represented females and larger I. bernissartensis represented males of the same species, but this hypothesis was later discarded.
facts.quote: En un tiempo se llegó a sugerir que I. mantelli o I. atherfieldensis, actualmente Dollodon y Mantellisaurus, respectivamente, de Bernissart representaban hembras y los más grandes y robustos I. bernissartensis machos de una misma especie, pero se descartó posteriormente

facts.statement: A 2017 analysis revealed high levels of individual variation in I. bernissartensis across limbs, shoulder, arm, thumb claw, pelvis, thigh, shin, and spine.
facts.quote: Un análisis de 2017 mostró que I. bernissartensis exhibe un gran nivel de variación individual tanto en sus extremidades, escápula , húmero, uña pulgar, ilion , isquion, fémur, tibia y columna vertebral

facts.statement: Individuals of I. bernissartensis generally fell into two categories based on whether their tail vertebrae had a groove on the underside and whether their thumb claws were large or small.
facts.quote: Además, este análisis encontró que los individuos de I. bernissartensis en general parecían caer en dos categorías en función de si sus vértebras de la cola tenían un surco en la parte inferior, y si sus garras del pulgar eran grandes o pequeñas

facts.quote: Parent group: Ankylopollexia

facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia
